Zastavna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Chernivtsi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews first settled in Zastavna in the early 18th century, growing from 17 people in 1774 to 100 by 1808; by the second half of the 19th century, the community supported three synagogues, a mikvah, and a Talmud Torah, and Jews held the position of mayor and other official posts. A Hebrew school opened in 1918, and Zionist organizations including WIZO and Beitar were active in the interwar period; the Jewish population reached 629 (12.3 percent) by 1930. This cemetery, established in 1870, was demolished during or after WWII; a 1993 memorial made from its own recovered gravestones now marks the site. Following the German-Romanian occupation of June 1941, the Jews of Zastavna and neighboring villages were imprisoned in a ghetto and deported to Transnistria that October; around 40 survivors returned after the war before later emigrating to Eretz Israel.
